profile.headline: Rendering Technologies
profile.geoLocationName: Los Angeles County, California, United States
profile.summary:
▪ Demonstrated ability to make good decisions when balancing constraints against requirements. 
▪ Ability to write simple, no-frills code, which doesn't introduce more complexity than necessary into a particular system. I tend to approach implementation tasks from a bottom up, data-oriented design mentality, paying close attention to the strengths and weaknesses of the target hardware. Able to "get things done". 
▪ Excellent large-scale code architecture sensibilities, in particular with writing robust scalable multi-threaded code. 
▪ Many years of experience with physically based lighting pipelines, real-time and offline, rasterized and ray-traced. 
▪ Windows, Linux, C++, C, Python, HLSL, ISPC, OptiX, Cuda, Direct3D, OpenGL, TBB, SIMD vectorization, USD, Hydra, imgui, Ptex, Embree, VTune, git.

positions.title: Staff Autopilot Software Engineer
positions.description: Working on simulating reality for FSD and Optimus.

positions.title: Sr. Staff Engineer
positions.description: Member of the Hyperion rendering team focusing on real-time GPU ray tracing.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Co-architect of DreamWorks Animation's new production ray-tracer named "MoonRay", which is being used to render all DreamWorks Animation films for the foreseeable future.
- Renderer scalability and longevity were a particular focus of mine which led me to drive in-house best practices and conventions, to ensure MoonRay could scale seamlessly up to multiple thousands of cores.
- Developed and executed a novel plan to make extensive use of traditionally untapped CPU vector hardware resources, resulting in up to a 2x speedup in render time. I presented an overview of this at the High Performance Graphics conference in 2017, see publications for more details.
- Other areas of the ray-tracer I designed and implemented with raw performance in mind were the queuing and sorting mechanisms, the threading architecture, the tiled progressive, real-time and batch mode render drivers, the memory allocation subsystems, the texture sampling subsystem, the profiling subsystem, and physical lights.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Drastically reduced "time to first pixel" for lighters iterating on complex scenes by updating much of the asset conditioning pipeline so that it allowed incremental building and executed in a fully multi-threaded fashion.
- Achieved over a 2 orders of magnitude speed-up over the previous implementation by rewriting the core graph evaluation code of our in-house lighting tool called "Torch". What was an overnight process could now be executed in minutes. This work later received a DreamWorks Technical Achievement Award.

positions.title: College student
positions.description: Took classes to revise calculus and linear algebra.

positions.title: Principal Programmer
positions.description:
- Played a large part in the design and architecture of our next-gen cross-platform rendering engine across the PS3, xbox360, and PC. This was built from the ground up with a focus on highly dynamic worlds, physically based HDR lighting and realistic material reflectance.
- Rendering team lead. Managed a team of graphics programmers, liaised with artists and other content creators to gather requirements and build consensus.
- Multi-threaded, re-projection based dynamic software occlusion pipeline.
- VPL based prototypes for global illumination.
- Games shipped: Resistance 3.

positions.title: Senior Programmer
positions.description:
- General tasks included implementing a linear light pipeline in our old engine and helping artists transition over to work in this new environment.
- Rendering tasks included switching our forward renderer to deferred, low-level RSX profiling, debugging and optimization, implementing a high quality SSAO scheme based on re-projecting the previous frame's results on the GPU, and real-time caustics on SPU.
- Tools based work included writing a custom Maya UV unwrapping plugin, the light mapping pipeline, and a PERL based shader building pipeline, which would automatically try out hundreds of permutations of each shader and pick the most optimal.
- Games shipped: Resistance 1 and 2, Ratchet and Clank Future: Tools of Destruction, Ratchet and Clank Future: A Crack in Time.

positions.title: Programmer
positions.description:
- Responsible for many aspects of our renderer including low-level state management, the material system, runtime shader generation, the geometry, skeletal and material LOD systems, water rendering, full screen post processing effects, and foliage rendering.
- Designed and implemented all aspects of the audio engine. Worked closely with the sound designers to find solutions for our audio requirements, which included supporting very large amounts of audio content, transparent lip-sync on all speech, and exposing all functionality to designers in an intuitive fashion.
- Responsible for our animation pipeline including integrating Granny into our code base, writing MEL scripts and creating user-friendly previewing tools.
- Games shipped: Oddworld: Stranger's Wrath.

positions.title: Technical Director
positions.description:
- Architect and primary implementer of our internal graphics engine on the Xbox1 and PC.
- Oversaw and guided lead programmers with their respective projects.
- Set and maintained internal coding conventions and standards.

positions.title: Programmer
positions.description:
- Worked on a small team with two other programmers. Among other responsibilities, I wrote the ASM polygon rendering code, the scripting language, the audio engine, and the 3DS MAX exporter/tool chain.
- Games shipped: Speed Freaks / Speed Punks (US). A highly regarded cartoon/combat style racing game published by Sony on the PS1.

honors.title: DreamWorks Technical Achievement Award
honors.description: Recognition of early work done to optimize our in-house lighting tool named "Torch".
